speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs in light of growing religious radicalisation of youths in the region (a) what plans are in place to further engage religious organisations in Singapore to look out for youths-at-risk; (b) whether informal religious groups are tracked for potential risks; and (c) whether there are controls over visits by radical overseas religious leaders to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They are also tailoring their messages and engagement platforms, including social media platforms, to better reach out to youths.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Besides engaging youths, we have to take other steps to reduce radical religious influences in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Even if they do not say these things in Singapore, we cannot allow them to build up their following in Singapore because, fundamentally, those teachings will destroy our society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Yam also asked whether informal religious groups are tracked for potential risks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With regard to control of visits by overseas religious leaders, is there a protocol or Standard Operating Procedure for the approval of the visit pass?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In a recent incident involving a particular preacher, publicity had already gone out for his visit to Singapore before his visit was denied by the authorities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The protocol is a very straightforward and transparent one.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We cannot control the publicity that others may give.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Member did not mention a name but he is probably referring to a gentleman who, if we look up on the Internet, has said, for example, that it is absolutely wrong to wish Christians "Merry Christmas".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Page: 6 It is contrary to the teachings of the Quran.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, of course, he says it in much more powerful terms than the way I can put it to you.
